report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Deadline fixed (3 months) and requirements well-defined with signed-off success metrics, but team composition (3 devs + 1 PM for 40 users across two teams) and real-time data refresh complexity warrant sprint-based validation cycles within predictive phase structure.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Add real-time reporting and alerting capabilities to the existing customer analytics dashboard to eliminate manual report generation.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Customer Success Team (15 people) and Sales Team (25 people)
project_understanding.trigger: CSMs spending 10 hours/week on manual report generation; leadership mandate for automation.
success_definition: CSMs can create custom reports in < 5 minutes
90% of scheduled reports delivered on time
supporting_quotes: Customer success managers are spending 10 hours/week manually generating reports. Leadership wants automated dashboards.
Add real-time reporting and alerting capabilities to our existing customer analytics dashboard.
CSMs can create custom reports in < 5 minutes; 90% of scheduled reports delivered on time; Alert response time < 1 hour

assumption_log.what: Security implementation assumes SSO is the sole authentication mechanism; no additional role-based access control (RBAC) or data-level permissions required beyond SSO group membership.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies 'Must integrate with existing authentication (SSO)' but does not detail authorization scope. For internal tools with two known beneficiary teams, SSO group-based access is standard default.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 (Quality Planning); security scope is a quality attribute that affects architecture if wrong.
assumption_log.consequence: If granular RBAC or data-level permissions are required (e.g., CSMs see only their customers, Sales see only their accounts), authentication layer must be re-architected post-build, delaying launch by 2–3 weeks.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Faster build using SSO group membership for access control. Risks: If fine-grained authorization is required, re-architecture needed; team must validate with stakeholders before Phase 2.

assumption_log.what: Data retention policy of 2 years applies to all customer analytics data; no separate retention tiers (e.g., raw events vs. aggregated reports) or compliance-driven deletion workflows required.
assumption_log.why: Input states '2 years' but does not specify scope (all data, reports only, raw events only) or deletion mechanism. For internal analytics, uniform 2-year retention with automated purge is standard.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 (Scope Definition); data retention is a non-functional requirement affecting storage architecture and compliance.
assumption_log.consequence: If compliance requires tiered retention (e.g., PII purged at 1 year, aggregates at 2 years) or audit trails preserved longer, database schema and purge job must be redesigned, adding 1–2 weeks to Phase 2.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Simpler schema and purge automation using uniform 2-year TTL. Risks: If tiered retention or compliance audit trails required, re-design needed; validate with Legal/Compliance before Phase 2.

assumption_log.what: Real-time data refresh every 15 minutes is acceptable latency for all KPI widgets; no sub-minute refresh or streaming data requirements.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies '15 minutes' as refresh interval. For internal dashboards used by CSMs and Sales (not real-time trading or incident response), 15-minute batches are standard and reduce infrastructure complexity.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 6.4 (Schedule Development); latency assumption affects batch job design and infrastructure.
assumption_log.consequence: If stakeholders require sub-5-minute refresh for alert-driven workflows, batch architecture must shift to event-driven streaming (Kafka/Kinesis), adding 2–3 weeks and increasing infrastructure cost by ~30%.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Simpler batch-based ETL using cron jobs; lower infrastructure cost. Risks: If sub-minute latency required, streaming architecture needed; validate refresh SLA with CSM/Sales leads before Phase 2.

hard.compliance: Data retention: 2 years; SSO authentication required

nfr.security: SSO authentication integration; authorization scope TBD (see A1)
nfr.data_retention: 2 years (scope and tiering TBD; see A2)

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Who is the Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization and sprint-level scope decisions during Phase 2–3?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Hybrid SDLC requires a single PO to manage sprint backlog and validate working software with stakeholders; without clear ownership, sprint cycles will stall on scope disputes.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Does the existing dashboard have a data warehouse or reporting database, or will custom reports query the production OLTP database?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Query performance and data freshness architecture depend on this; if production DB is used, report queries may impact operational performance, requiring caching or ETL layer design.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Are there granular authorization requirements (e.g., CSMs see only their customers, Sales see only their accounts), or is team-level access via SSO groups sufficient?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Assumption A1 defaults to SSO group-based access; if row-level security or customer-scoped filtering is required, authentication/authorization layer must be re-architected.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: What is the expected volume of scheduled reports (daily, weekly, monthly) and concurrent users during peak usage?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Email scheduling and alert notification infrastructure (PagerDuty integration) must handle peak load; without volume estimates, job queue and notification service capacity cannot be sized.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Is the 2-year data retention policy uniform across all data types (raw events, aggregated reports, audit logs), or are there tiered retention requirements?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Assumption A2 defaults to uniform 2-year retention; if compliance or audit requirements mandate longer retention for logs or shorter for PII, database schema and purge automation must be redesigned.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: What is the acceptable latency for alert notifications (e.g., must PagerDuty alert fire within 5 minutes of threshold breach, or is 15-minute batch acceptable)?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Assumption A3 defaults to 15-minute batch refresh; if sub-5-minute alert latency is required, event-driven architecture (Kafka/Kinesis) must replace batch jobs, adding 2–3 weeks and infrastructure cost.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Is there a budget constraint, or is the 3-month deadline the primary constraint?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Budget unknown; if infrastructure or third-party service costs (e.g., PagerDuty, email service) are constrained, cost-optimization decisions (e.g., batch vs. streaming, caching strategy) must be made early.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend Developer and Product Manager must be dedicated (not shared) across Phases 1–4; Frontend Developer can absorb Phase 1 audit work with 2 days slack.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: Existing dashboard audit completed
Regression risk assessment documented
Data architecture decision (OLTP vs. warehouse) finalized
Authorization scope validated with stakeholders
Requirements finalized and signed off

tasks.name: Audit existing dashboard architecture and identify regression risks
tasks.definition_of_done: Audit report documents current system components, data flow, existing test coverage, and 5+ regression risk areas with mitigation strategies.

tasks.name: Validate authorization scope with Product Manager and stakeholders
tasks.definition_of_done: Written confirmation from CSM and Sales leads on whether SSO group-based access (Assumption A1) is sufficient or row-level security required; signed off by Product Manager.

tasks.name: Document backward compatibility requirements for existing features
tasks.definition_of_done: Compatibility matrix lists all existing dashboard features and specifies which must remain unchanged during new feature rollout.

tasks.name: Validate data retention and tiering requirements with Legal/Compliance
tasks.definition_of_done: Written confirmation from Legal/Compliance on whether uniform 2-year retention (Assumption A2) applies to all data types or tiered retention required; signed off.

tasks.name: Design data architecture for custom reports and refresh strategy
tasks.definition_of_done: Architecture document specifies whether custom reports query OLTP or warehouse, batch refresh frequency (15-min default per A3), caching strategy, and query performance targets.

tasks.name: Create detailed API specification for custom report generation endpoint
tasks.definition_of_done: OpenAPI 3.0 spec documents request/response schema, query parameters (date range, metrics, filters), error codes, and rate limits for report generation.

tasks.name: Design UI mockups for custom report builder and alert configuration
tasks.definition_of_done: Figma/Sketch mockups show custom report builder (date range, metric selection, filters), alert threshold UI, and schedule delivery form; reviewed and approved by Product Manager.

phases.name: Core Development (Sprint Cycles)
milestones: Sprint 1: Authentication and dashboard data refresh working
Sprint 2: Custom report generation API complete
Sprint 3: Report export (PDF/CSV) and scheduling backend complete
Sprint 4: Alert configuration and PagerDuty integration complete
Core features implemented and internal demo completed

tasks.name: Implement SSO authentication integration with existing auth service
tasks.definition_of_done: SSO login flow works end-to-end; user session tokens validated; group membership extracted and stored in session context.

tasks.name: Build 15-minute batch ETL job to refresh dashboard data
tasks.definition_of_done: Cron job runs every 15 minutes; pulls latest data from source (OLTP or warehouse per T5 decision); updates dashboard cache; logs execution time and row counts.

tasks.name: Implement custom report query builder backend (date range, metrics, filters)
tasks.definition_of_done: API endpoint accepts report parameters; constructs and executes SQL query; returns results in < 5 minutes for typical CSM use case (30-day range, 5 metrics).

tasks.name: Build custom report UI form (date range, metric selection, filters)
tasks.definition_of_done: React form component renders metric checkboxes, date picker, filter dropdowns; submits to T10 API; displays loading state and results table.

tasks.name: Implement PDF and CSV export for reports
tasks.definition_of_done: Export endpoint generates PDF (with branding) and CSV; includes report metadata (date range, filters applied); file downloads in < 10 seconds.

tasks.name: Build report scheduling backend (cron job, email queue, delivery logic)
tasks.definition_of_done: Scheduled reports stored in database; cron job triggers at configured times; report generated and queued for email delivery; delivery status tracked.

tasks.name: Implement email delivery integration (SMTP or third-party service)
tasks.definition_of_done: Email service sends scheduled reports with PDF/CSV attachment; delivery logs recorded; bounce/failure handling implemented.

tasks.name: Build report scheduling UI (frequency, recipients, delivery time)
tasks.definition_of_done: React form allows users to select report, set frequency (daily/weekly/monthly), add recipients, choose delivery time; submits to T13 API.

tasks.name: Implement alert threshold configuration backend
tasks.definition_of_done: API stores alert rules (metric, threshold, operator, notification channel); validation ensures thresholds are numeric and channels are valid.

tasks.name: Build alert evaluation engine (periodic check against thresholds)
tasks.definition_of_done: Cron job runs every 15 minutes; evaluates all active alerts against latest dashboard data; triggers notification if threshold breached; deduplicates repeated alerts.

tasks.name: Integrate PagerDuty for alert notifications
tasks.definition_of_done: Alert engine calls PagerDuty API to create incidents; incident includes metric name, threshold, current value, and dashboard link; API key stored securely.

tasks.name: Build alert configuration UI (threshold, metric, notification channel)
tasks.definition_of_done: React form allows users to select metric, set threshold value, choose operator (>, <, =), select notification channel (PagerDuty, email); submits to T16 API.

tasks.name: Implement feature flag strategy for gradual rollout
tasks.definition_of_done: Feature flags control visibility of custom reports, scheduling, and alerts; flags can be toggled per user or team without code deployment.

phases.name: Integration & Edge Cases (Sprint Cycles)
milestones: Sprint 5: Regression test suite passes; all integrations tested
Sprint 6: Edge cases handled; performance benchmarks met
All integrations tested and security review completed

tasks.name: Build regression test suite for existing dashboard features
tasks.definition_of_done: Automated test suite covers all existing dashboard widgets, filters, and exports; baseline performance metrics recorded; tests run in < 10 minutes.

tasks.name: Execute full regression test pass against existing features
tasks.definition_of_done: All regression tests pass; no new failures introduced; performance metrics within 5% of baseline; defects logged and triaged.

tasks.name: Test custom report generation with edge cases (large date ranges, many metrics)
tasks.definition_of_done: Reports generated for 2-year date range, 20+ metrics, complex filters; execution time logged; timeout and memory limits validated.

tasks.name: Test report scheduling and email delivery at scale (100+ scheduled reports)
tasks.definition_of_done: 100 scheduled reports created; delivery job runs without queue overflow; all emails delivered within 5 minutes of scheduled time; no duplicates.

tasks.name: Test alert evaluation and PagerDuty integration under load
tasks.definition_of_done: 50+ alerts evaluated every 15 minutes; PagerDuty incidents created correctly; alert deduplication prevents duplicate incidents; latency < 2 minutes.

tasks.name: Conduct security review and penetration testing
tasks.definition_of_done: Security review covers authentication, authorization, SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, data exposure; penetration test report generated; critical findings remediated.

tasks.name: Document rollback plan for new features
tasks.definition_of_done: Rollback procedure documents how to disable custom reports, scheduling, and alerts via feature flags; tested in staging environment.

tasks.name: Performance comparison: new features vs. baseline
tasks.definition_of_done: Report compares dashboard load time, report generation time, and alert evaluation latency before and after new features; variance < 10%.

phases.name: QA & Testing
milestones: UAT with CSM and Sales teams completed
All critical bugs resolved
Documentation and runbooks written
Training materials prepared

tasks.name: Prepare UAT environment and test data
tasks.definition_of_done: UAT environment mirrors production; test data includes 6 months of sample customer analytics; 10 pre-configured test reports and alerts ready.

tasks.name: Conduct UAT with Customer Success Team (5 users, 2 days)
tasks.definition_of_done: 5 CSMs test custom reports, scheduling, and alerts; feedback documented; critical issues logged; sign-off obtained on core workflows.

tasks.name: Conduct UAT with Sales Team (5 users, 2 days)
tasks.definition_of_done: 5 Sales reps test custom reports, scheduling, and alerts; feedback documented; critical issues logged; sign-off obtained on core workflows.

tasks.name: Triage and fix critical bugs from UAT
tasks.definition_of_done: All P0 and P1 bugs fixed and verified; regression tests pass; UAT sign-off obtained from both teams.

tasks.name: Write API documentation and developer runbook
tasks.definition_of_done: API docs include endpoint specs, authentication, error codes, rate limits; runbook covers deployment, monitoring, troubleshooting, and rollback.

tasks.name: Write user documentation and quick-start guide
tasks.definition_of_done: User guide covers custom report creation, scheduling, alert configuration with screenshots; quick-start guide (1 page) for new users.

tasks.name: Create training materials and record demo video
tasks.definition_of_done: Training deck covers all new features; 10-minute demo video recorded; materials shared with CSM and Sales leads for internal training.

tasks.name: Set up monitoring and alerting for production dashboard
tasks.definition_of_done: Monitoring covers API latency, error rates, batch job execution, email delivery, PagerDuty integration; alerts configured for SLA breaches.

tasks.name: Prepare data retention and purge automation
tasks.definition_of_done: Purge job deletes data older than 2 years (per A2); runs monthly; logs retention policy compliance; tested in staging.

phases.name: Deployment & Handoff
milestones: Production deployment completed
Smoke testing in production passed
Go-live sign-off obtained

tasks.name: Deploy to production (feature flags disabled initially)
tasks.definition_of_done: Code deployed to production; feature flags for custom reports, scheduling, alerts set to OFF; database migrations applied; no errors in logs.

tasks.name: Execute smoke tests in production
tasks.definition_of_done: Smoke tests verify SSO login, dashboard load, existing features work; no critical errors; performance metrics within SLA.

tasks.name: Enable feature flags and monitor for 2 hours
tasks.definition_of_done: Feature flags enabled for custom reports, scheduling, alerts; monitoring dashboard shows no errors; error rate < 0.1%; go-live sign-off obtained.

risk_register.description: If authorization scope (granular RBAC vs. SSO group-based) is not validated before Phase 2, and stakeholders require row-level security or customer-scoped filtering, then authentication/authorization layer must be re-architected post-build, delaying launch by 2-3 weeks and consuming critical path time.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 begins without written sign-off on authorization scope; stakeholder requests granular access control during sprint review
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct authorization scope workshop with CSM and Sales leads before Phase 2 kickoff; document and sign off on whether SSO group-based access or row-level security is required; add validation task to Phase 1 gate
risk_register.contingency: If granular RBAC discovered mid-Phase 2, pause feature development; re-architect authentication layer with Backend Developer; compress non-critical features to recover schedule

risk_register.description: If alert latency requirements are not clarified before Phase 2, and stakeholders require sub-5-minute alert delivery instead of 15-minute batch refresh, then event-driven architecture (Kafka/Kinesis) must replace batch jobs, adding 2-3 weeks to Phase 2-3 and increasing infrastructure cost.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint review reveals stakeholder expectation for real-time alerts; PagerDuty integration testing shows 15-minute latency unacceptable for CSM workflows
risk_register.mitigation: Validate alert latency SLA with CSM and Sales leads before Phase 2; document acceptable latency in requirements; confirm 15-minute batch refresh meets business need; add latency acceptance criteria to UC7 definition
risk_register.contingency: If sub-5-minute latency required, pivot to event-driven architecture; allocate Backend Developer to Kafka/Kinesis setup; defer non-critical reporting features to Phase 4

risk_register.description: If the existing dashboard lacks a dedicated data warehouse or reporting database, and custom reports query the production OLTP database directly, then report generation and scheduled refresh jobs may degrade operational performance, causing dashboard slowness and alert delays.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 audit reveals no reporting database; custom report queries against production DB show > 2-second latency; CSM reports slow dashboard during peak hours
risk_register.mitigation: Complete Phase 1 data architecture audit before Phase 2; confirm whether reporting database or ETL layer exists; if not, design caching or read replica strategy in Phase 1; add performance testing task to Phase 2
risk_register.contingency: If production DB queries cause performance issues, implement read replica or in-memory cache (Redis) for dashboard widgets; defer complex custom reports to Phase 4; add query optimization task to critical path

risk_register.description: If Product Owner role is not assigned before Phase 2, and backlog prioritization or sprint-level scope decisions lack a single decision-maker, then sprint cycles will stall on scope disputes between CSM and Sales stakeholders, delaying feature delivery.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint planning begins without named PO; conflicting feature requests from CSM and Sales teams; sprint review blocked on scope decision
risk_register.mitigation: Assign Product Owner (likely PM) with explicit authority for backlog prioritization and sprint scope decisions before Phase 2 kickoff; document PO role and decision-making authority in project charter; establish weekly PO sync with stakeholders
risk_register.contingency: If PO unavailable, escalate to project sponsor for tie-breaking authority; implement MoSCoW prioritization framework to reduce scope disputes; add PO availability as Phase 2 gate criterion

risk_register.description: If PagerDuty integration is not tested with expected report volume and concurrent alert load before Phase 3, and peak usage exceeds PagerDuty rate limits or email service capacity, then alert delivery will fail or be delayed, missing the < 1 hour alert response SLA.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 load testing reveals alert queue backlog; PagerDuty rate limit errors in logs; CSM reports missed alerts during peak hours
risk_register.mitigation: Clarify expected volume of scheduled reports and concurrent users during Phase 1 open questions; size job queue and notification service capacity in Phase 2 design; add load testing for alert delivery to Phase 3 plan; confirm PagerDuty and email service SLAs
risk_register.contingency: If capacity exceeded, implement alert batching or priority queuing; upgrade PagerDuty plan or add secondary notification channel; defer low-priority alerts to Phase 4

risk_register.description: If data retention policy scope is not clarified before Phase 2, and compliance or audit requirements mandate tiered retention (e.g., PII purged at 1 year, aggregates at 2 years, audit logs longer), then database schema and purge automation must be redesigned, adding 1-2 weeks to Phase 2.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 design review reveals compliance requirement for tiered retention; Legal/Compliance feedback requests longer audit log retention; database schema must be refactored
risk_register.mitigation: Validate data retention policy scope with Legal/Compliance before Phase 2; confirm whether uniform 2-year retention or tiered retention is required; document retention tiers and purge automation in Phase 2 design; add compliance review gate
risk_register.contingency: If tiered retention required, redesign database schema and purge jobs; allocate Backend Developer to retention logic; defer non-critical features to Phase 4

risk_register.description: If Backend Developer is unavailable or context-switches to other projects during critical path tasks (T2, T5, T9, T13, T18, T22, T26), then authentication, data refresh, alerting, and deployment will be delayed, pushing launch past 2025-04-10 deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Backend Developer allocated to competing project; critical path task blocked waiting for Backend Developer; Phase 2-3 sprint velocity drops below plan
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm Backend Developer is 100% dedicated to project through Phase 4; document in resource plan and secure commitment from engineering manager; establish weekly capacity check-in; flag any competing commitments immediately
risk_register.contingency: If Backend Developer unavailable, escalate to project sponsor for resource reallocation; identify backup Backend Developer for knowledge transfer; compress non-critical features to recover schedule

risk_register.description: If Product Manager is unavailable or context-switches to other projects during critical path tasks (T1, T2, T5, T9, T13, T18, T22, T26), then project planning, stakeholder alignment, and sprint reviews will be delayed, stalling the hybrid SDLC cycle.
risk_register.trigger: PM allocated to competing initiative; sprint planning or review cancelled; stakeholder alignment meetings missed; critical path task blocked
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm PM is 100% dedicated to project through Phase 4; document in resource plan and secure commitment from management; establish weekly availability check-in; block calendar for sprint ceremonies and stakeholder syncs
risk_register.contingency: If PM unavailable, escalate to project sponsor; identify backup PM for knowledge transfer; delegate sprint facilitation to Backend Developer or external Scrum Master

risk_register.description: If custom report generation performance is not validated against the < 5 minute SLA before Phase 3, and complex queries with large date ranges or multiple filters exceed latency targets, then CSM workflow will not meet success criteria, requiring query optimization or caching redesign.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 UAT reveals custom report generation > 5 minutes for large datasets; CSM feedback indicates reports too slow for workflow; performance testing shows query latency unacceptable
risk_register.mitigation: Add performance testing for custom report generation to Phase 2 design; define query optimization strategy (indexing, caching, query limits) in Phase 2; test with realistic data volumes and filter combinations; add performance acceptance criteria to UC3
risk_register.contingency: If latency exceeds SLA, implement query result caching or pagination; add database indexing or query optimization; defer complex filter combinations to Phase 4

risk_register.description: If success criteria for 'CSMs can create custom reports in < 5 minutes' is not operationalized (e.g., measured from UI interaction start to report download, or from report definition to email delivery), then Phase 3 UAT may dispute whether success criteria are met, delaying sign-off.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 UAT begins without clear definition of '< 5 minutes'; CSM and team disagree on measurement point; sign-off delayed pending clarification
risk_register.mitigation: Define and document success criteria measurement methodology before Phase 2; specify whether '< 5 minutes' includes UI interaction, backend processing, or email delivery; add acceptance criteria to UC3 and UC5; validate with CSM lead
risk_register.contingency: If measurement disputed, conduct joint timing test with CSM; adjust success criteria if measurement methodology was ambiguous; document agreed measurement for Phase 3 UAT

risk_register.description: If SSO authentication integration is not tested with the actual SSO provider before Phase 2, and SSO group membership or token format differs from assumptions, then user authentication will fail or require re-implementation, delaying Phase 2 feature development.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 development begins; SSO integration test fails due to token format mismatch; authentication layer must be re-implemented; Phase 2 sprint blocked
risk_register.mitigation: Complete SSO integration testing in Phase 1 audit; confirm SSO group membership structure and token format with IT/Security; implement SSO mock or sandbox before Phase 2; add SSO integration acceptance test to Phase 1 gate
risk_register.contingency: If SSO integration fails, implement alternative authentication (LDAP, OAuth) as fallback; allocate Backend Developer to re-implement authentication layer; defer feature development until authentication resolved

risk_register.description: If 15-minute dashboard refresh interval is not validated as acceptable for alert-driven workflows, and CSMs expect real-time KPI updates to trigger immediate action, then alert response time SLA (< 1 hour) may be unachievable with batch refresh, requiring architecture change.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint review reveals CSM expectation for real-time dashboard updates; alert response time testing shows 15-minute refresh causes SLA miss; stakeholder requests sub-minute refresh
risk_register.mitigation: Validate 15-minute refresh interval with CSM and Sales leads before Phase 2; confirm acceptable latency for alert-driven workflows; document refresh SLA in requirements; test alert response time with 15-minute batch in Phase 2
risk_register.contingency: If real-time refresh required, pivot to event-driven architecture; implement WebSocket or polling for dashboard updates; defer batch reporting to Phase 4

risk_register.description: If 'nice-to-have' features (e.g., advanced filtering, custom dashboards, multi-user report sharing) are not explicitly excluded from Phase 2-3 scope, then scope creep may consume critical path time, delaying core features and pushing launch past deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint planning includes stakeholder requests for advanced features; scope expands beyond MVP; critical path tasks delayed; sprint velocity drops
risk_register.mitigation: Define MVP scope explicitly in Phase 1 gate; document which features are Phase 2-3 (MVP) vs. Phase 4 (enhancements); establish change control process for scope additions; prioritize using MoSCoW framework; review scope at each sprint review
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs, conduct scope negotiation with stakeholders; defer lower-priority features to Phase 4; compress non-critical tasks to recover schedule

risk_register.description: If infrastructure or third-party service costs (PagerDuty, email service, database, caching) are not budgeted or constrained, and cost-optimization decisions (batch vs. streaming, caching strategy) are deferred, then Phase 2-3 infrastructure design may exceed budget, requiring re-architecture.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 infrastructure design reveals high cost for streaming architecture or premium PagerDuty plan; budget constraint discovered; cost-optimization required
risk_register.mitigation: Clarify budget constraint before Phase 2; estimate infrastructure costs for batch vs. streaming architecture; select cost-optimal design (batch preferred unless latency requires streaming); add cost review to Phase 2 gate
risk_register.contingency: If budget exceeded, pivot to batch architecture; negotiate PagerDuty volume discount; implement caching to reduce database load; defer premium features to Phase 4

risk_register.description: If email service integration (for scheduled report delivery) is not tested with expected volume before Phase 3, and email delivery fails or is rate-limited, then scheduled report SLA (90% on-time delivery) will not be met.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 load testing reveals email service rate limiting; scheduled reports fail to deliver; CSM reports missing reports; email service quota exceeded
risk_register.mitigation: Clarify expected volume of scheduled reports during Phase 1 open questions; select email service with sufficient capacity (e.g., SendGrid, AWS SES); add load testing for email delivery to Phase 3 plan; confirm email service SLA
risk_register.contingency: If email delivery fails, implement retry logic with exponential backoff; upgrade email service plan; add secondary email provider as fallback; defer low-priority scheduled reports

staffing_plan.notes: PM is critical path owner for T2, T4, T30, T31, T34, T35. Must be 100% dedicated (not shared) through Phase 4. Allocation 13% of 600 total project hours meets PMBOK 9.2 PM oversight rule (10-15%). No backup specified; projects >3 months require named backup — flagged as Resource Risk R8.

Backend Developer owns critical path tasks T1, T5, T9, T13, T18, T22, T26. Must be 100% dedicated (not shared) through Phase 4. Allocation 46.7% reflects heavy Phase 2-3 load (core development, integration, security). No backup specified; projects >3 months require named backup — flagged as Resource Risk R7. Single person covering multiple critical roles (architecture, development, security, deployment); overlap flagged as Resource Risk.

Frontend Developer owns T7, T11, T15, T19 (UI forms and components). Phase 1 audit work (T7) has 2-day slack; not on critical path. Allocation 15% allows capacity for other projects. No critical path backup required.

QA Engineer owns critical path task T22 (regression test execution). Total QA hours (150) = 25% of total dev hours (280 Backend + 90 Frontend = 370), meeting PMBOK 8.2 minimum QA allocation rule. Phase 3-4 heavy involvement (testing, UAT, smoke tests). No backup specified; projects >3 months require named backup — flagged as Resource Risk.
Solution Architect owns T1 (audit existing dashboard). Phase 1 only; front-loaded role. Allocation 2.7% reflects short engagement. Critical path task but Phase 1 gate; no ongoing backup required.
